   ```ts
   import type { GeospatialCamera, GeospatialLimits } from "@babylonjs/lite";

   /**
    * Point the camera at a map mode's GeospatialLimits.
    *
    * From then on the camera clamps any radius (zoom) or yaw (heading)
    * write against these limits, and camera.limits reports them.
    * Calling it again with another mode's limits switches the ranges.
    */
   export function useModeLimits(camera: GeospatialCamera, limits: GeospatialLimits): void {
       // Assigning the limits object is what makes the camera clamp future
       // radius/yaw writes against it (camera-notes.md #37). The mode's
       // object is never mutated, so holding the reference is safe.
       camera.limits = limits;

       // A limits change only clamps writes that actually change a value,
       // so a pose that is already outside the new range would stay there
       // until the app writes something different. Clamp the current pose
       // now (radius first, per #7) so the camera is inside the mode's
       // ranges immediately.
       const radius = Math.min(Math.max(camera.radius, limits.radiusMin), limits.radiusMax);
       if (radius !== camera.radius) {
           camera.radius = radius;
       }

       const yaw = Math.min(Math.max(camera.yaw, limits.yawMin), limits.yawMax);
       if (yaw !== camera.yaw) {
           camera.yaw = yaw;
       }
   }
   ```
